text:
[LTAC.3.4] The follow-up rule is named as [LTAC.8.1] states. Its one
pattern matches a fact `t` of the timer schema under the guard `monotonic_ns() >= t.fire_at`, so it
matches the timer whose `fire_at` is at or before the current clock. Its RHS
is the `after` clause's action list, followed by the retraction of `t`.

The retraction has no author syntax: the timer schema's lifecycle is
explicit, and the compiler emits the retraction directly into the synthetic
rule. Neither this
rule nor its schema is writable by an author — `retract` is not one
of the action heads ([LGRA.10.1]) — which is why `after` is a
language form rather than a macro over one.


**A `logical` emit in the body is refused** ([LLOG.11.9]): the follow-up
retracts the timer, so the activation that would justify the fact ends
inside its own firing.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__alphas
idris.note: The follow-up program's alphas: the timer schema its one pattern matches. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__born
idris.note: The follow-up's activation as a tick makes it. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due
idris.note: `monotonic_ns() >= t.fire_at`, the follow-up's single positive pattern's guard, as a timed test.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due_b
idris.note: The guard for one timer, a predicate of the clock.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due_is_the_gate
idris.note: The follow-up's test at a timer is that timer's gate, at every clock and whatever the token. Computed.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__follow_up_rules
idris.note: THE FOLLOW-UP RULE: the timer schema's single positive pattern under the gate, then the retraction. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__net
idris.note: The follow-up's chain and the timer alpha. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__program
idris.note: THE PROGRAM: the follow-up alone, the timer kind explicit. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__state
idris.note: The follow-up's quiescent state at a clock. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__tick_literal
idris.note: The follow-up's LHS re-evaluated at a tick: the timer matched when its `fire_at` is at or before the clock.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__ticked
idris.note: The follow-up as a tick leaves it. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__timed
idris.note: THE TIMED TESTS, by ordinal: the follow-up's gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__wm
idris.note: The timer live until its follow-up retracts it; gone after. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__gone_is_an_instance
idris.note: ONE-SHOT at the one-shot history, through the theorem: the clock reaches `fire_at`, so the timer is not in working memory after. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__gone_once_due
idris.note: The follow-up's retraction, seen after any history that reaches `fire_at`.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__idle_net
idris.note: The follow-up's network with nothing pending. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__retract_timer
idris.note: The retraction the compiler emits into the synthetic rule, with no author syntax: the RHS's last action.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__step_fires
idris.note: The follow-up matches the due timer, runs its action list, and retracts the timer.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick
idris.note: The follow-up rule, over any tick history: it fires when the clock first reaches `fire_at`.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__timer_pump
idris.note: The follow-up, pumped at a tick: matches the timer whose `fire_at` is at or before the clock, fires, retracts it.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__lower
idris.note: One follow-up per clause, on its timer, with the body and the retraction. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__lower_tests
idris.note: THE TIMED TESTS the lowering gives with the rules: the parent's own, then each follow-up's guard. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__born_timed
idris.note: THE ACTIVATION A RE-TIME MAKES of one timer: the timer's match, unfired, when the gate was shut at the old clock and is open at the new; none otherwise. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__chain_timed
idris.note: THE FOLLOW-UP'S CHAIN at a clock over the timer's stamp: the one node with the gate re-timed to the clock, its activations, the retraction. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due_stamped
idris.note: THE GUARD AS A GATE: Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `dwell >= d` over the stamp table, the form the theorems take -- `t.dwell` read off the candidate's entry stamp, compared as naturals. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due_stamped_monotonic
idris.note: THE GATE FORM IS A MONOTONIC GATE at every stamp table: it reads the monotonic sample and the stamps, nothing of the wall. C2's hypothesis, inhabited; a TRANSCRIPTION of Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `dwell_gate_monotonic`, said so.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__follow_up
idris.note: THE FOLLOW-UP RULE as this clause has it: one pattern on the timer under the guard, the body then the retraction. Its name is [LTAC.8.1]'s, `$<rule>_after_<N>`, which the lowering writes; the model carries ordinals and no name. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard
idris.note: THE GUARD AS THE RUNNER BUILDS IT: Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's monotonic timed test of the expression, which reads no `now()`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_expr
idris.note: THE FOLLOW-UP'S GUARD AS THE LOWERING WRITES IT: `t.dwell >= dur` on the chain's one positive pattern, in the witnesses' units. `monotonic_ns() >= t.fire_at` with `fire_at` the stamp plus the duration. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_forms_agree
idris.note: THE TWO FORMS DECIDE ALIKE ON THE EXECUTED SHAPES: the runner's expression and the gate, on the timer stamped 0 with duration 5, both admit at the sample 6 and refuse at the sample 3. Computed. LESS than the clause: what the evaluator's Integer order gives on literals is run, not proved, as Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's `within` is.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_is_due
idris.note: THE GUARD IS THE GATE: for every stamp, every positive duration and every sample, `dwell >= S d` from the stamp `s` is `monotonic_ns() >= fire_at` with `fire_at = s + S d`, Rete/NetworkAfter.idr's gate. A Nat lemma, by induction on the stamp and the sample together; the duration is positive by [LTAC.7.1], which closes the case of a stamp ahead of the sample, where `dwell` saturates at zero.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__net_timed
idris.note: THE FOLLOW-UP'S NETWORK over a working memory at a clock: the timer alpha holding it and the one chain. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__retime_literal_timed
idris.note: The follow-up's node re-timed at the pump's entry, over the timer's stamp.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__state_timed
idris.note: THE QUIESCENT STATE OF ONE TIMER AT A CLOCK: the timer's working memory at that clock, no activation. What a cycle leaves, and what the theorems start from. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__tests_stamped
idris.note: THE TIMED TESTS of the follow-up alone, by ordinal: its gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__tick_literal_timed
idris.note: THE RE-TIME OF THE FOLLOW-UP at a new clock over the timer's stamp: the node takes the gate at the new clock; the timer's match is born unfired exactly when the gate was shut and is open; nothing is ended, a rising gate refusing nothing it admitted. Computed, over the four readings of the gate.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__timed_state
idris.note: A TIMED STATE of the follow-up: the clocked net over a working memory with no row and no deadline at a clock, the wall, the timer's stamp as the one entry, no tracker. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__wm_timed
idris.note: WORKING MEMORY OF ONE TIMER AT A CLOCK, quiescent: the timer stamped `s` with duration `d` live while its gate is shut at the clock, gone once the gate has opened -- the follow-up fired and retracted it. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__gone_once_due_timed
idris.note: The follow-up's retraction, seen after any history that reaches `fire_at`.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__idle_timed
idris.note: AN IDLE STATE: the follow-up with nothing to fire over a working memory at a clock. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__step_fires_timed
idris.note: The follow-up matches the due timer, runs its action list, and retracts the timer.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick_timed
idris.note: The follow-up rule, over any tick history on the Idris model's engine: it fires when the clock first reaches the stamp plus the duration.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__timer_cycle
idris.note: The follow-up, pumped at a tick: matches the timer whose stamp plus duration is at or before the clock, fires, retracts it.
